scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and automatically fix whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled starting August 2026, from ~600/month (Jun/Jul) to ~1200/month (Aug/Sep) (E-07).
Disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL meter-read bills (1785) over ESTIMATED bills (1240), contrary to an estimate-substitution narrative (E-01).
Field manual-read route completion is below target (0.88 vs 0.95) in Aug-Sep 2026, a separate shortfall that does not match the dispute's read-type pattern (E-03).
Dispute response times remain well within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA across 2440 tickets), so slow handling does not explain the surge (E-06).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180-1260/month starting August 2026 (E-07), with disputes attaching predominantly to bills built from ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED substitutions (1785 vs 1240, E-01). This pattern is consistent with a billing import validation rule change around August producing incorrect bills on actual-read accounts (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), ruling out tariff change (E-02), field manual-read gaps (E-01, E-03), and slow dispute response (E-06) as the driver.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response/handling gap, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets would resolve it (SH-CS framing).

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August is producing incorrect bills, driving the dispute increase.

H-AMI-FEED-FAILURE.statement: AMI register reads from the vendor (MDMS) are failing to deliver or validate correctly via H-MDMS-BILL, causing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual field meter-read collection or the H-FIELD-BILL handoff is incomplete/degraded (e.g., understaffing per SH-FIELD), causing estimated bills and disputes.

H-TICKET-MEASUREMENT-ARTIFACT.statement: The apparent doubling of dispute tickets since August reflects a CRM categorization or baseline-definition change rather than more actual billing errors.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: Billing import validation applies a high-consumption threshold rule that rejects legitimate AMI actual reads (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), producing incorrect bills for high-usage accounts and driving disputes.

H-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check compares raw register value to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling: none, so a scaling mismatch (not a genuine high-consumption event) may be misflagging and rejecting legitimate AMI actual reads per E-11.

U-RULECHANGE.decision_impact: If no rule change is confirmed, H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE is unsupported, the causal chain must be revisited, and SC-RULEID cannot be met.
U-RULECHANGE.resolution_path: Query billing-config (DA-RULES) rule change log and correlate change dates with disputed ACTUAL-read account bill dates.
U-RULECHANGE.safe_placeholder: Treat the rule-change mechanism as unconfirmed; limit the solution to diagnostic investigation and ticket triage support, no automated remediation, until DA-RULES confirms a specific change.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and automatically fix whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled starting August 2026, from ~600/month (Jun/Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug/Sep) (E-07).

Among disputed bills coded ESTIMATED, 1184 actually had legitimate AMI actual reads delivered before cutoff but rejected under billing_import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION despite being exported to billing, versus only 56 true non-delivery cases (E-11).
The 1184 rejected high-consumption reads are tagged firmware v4.2 (E-11), and v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register values in '0.1 m3' units distinct from v3.x's 'm3' units (E-13).

Billing import rule BV-17, implementing the high-consumption check, was deployed 2026-08-01 and compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling 'none' (E-12), coincident with the dispute-surge start.
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline (Jun/Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug/Sep 2026) (E-07), caused by billing import validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12), which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling "none"; this misreads firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1-m3-unit readings (rolled out 2026-06, E-13) as roughly 10x true consumption, causing 1184 legitimate high-consumption actual reads to be falsely rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and fall back to estimated billing (E-11), producing incorrect bills that drive the dispute surge.

These reads fall back to estimated billing, producing incorrect bills that drive the August/September dispute-volume doubling (E-07).

proposal.summary: SH-CS requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and fix wrong bills, after dispute volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month between Jun/Jul and Aug/Sep 2026 (E-07). Tariff change (E-02), field-read staffing gaps (E-03, E-05, E-09), and slow dispute handling (E-06) were tested and rejected as causes. An initial hypothesis that disputes concentrated on ACTUAL-read bills (E-01) was invalidated by E-11, showing ~1184 disputed ESTIMATED-labeled bills actually had legitimate AMI actual reads rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION). This traced to rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), comparing raw register values to m3 history with no unit scaling, misreading firmware v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 units (E-13); E-14 confirmed the same 1184 cases at account level. Problem definition PD-1@v2 states this as root cause, superseding PD-1@v1 (invalidated per DR-1, triggered by E-11). Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, covering only defect-scope confirmation (DA-RULES) and a CRM ticket-categorization audit (DA-TICKET), after CONDITIONAL_PASS at the DEFINE Gate. Full-population sizing/rebilling (DA-BILL) is excluded since VOB-U-SCOPE and VOB-U-REPROCESS remain open. No automated bill writes (K-BILLWRITE); agent cannot deploy the BV-17 fix itself.
key_points: Root cause (PD-1@v2): BV-17's unit-scaling-unaware check (E-12) misreads firmware v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 units (E-13), causing legitimate actual reads to be rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and billed as estimates, driving the dispute surge (E-07, E-11, E-14).
SH-CS's framing (CL-01) that an auto-answering agent could fix the cause was a hypothesis, not a fact; superseded once the mechanism was traced to a billing-config rule.
Three competing explanations were tested and rejected: tariff change (E-02, E-04), field-read staffing gap (E-03, E-05, E-09), slow dispute response (E-06).
